findings.summary: the sn-benchmark candidate-models default still names openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, which has no entry under [tool.imas-codex.llm.openrouter-pricing] and whose proxy route this same change renames to deepseek-v4-pro-0813 in imas_codex/config/litellm_config.yaml:113, so brief item 3's "every identifier a seat names has a cataloged price" and the new test's own stated property do not reach the fallback slate.

LATEST is a hand-maintained mirror of the seat list this change authored, so test_openrouter_seat_is_on_the_latest_release_of_its_line can catch a drift off that list but cannot establish that any entry is the newest release of its line; latestness is still asserted only by the cited created epochs in the evidence fragment.

the escalation rotation test's first assertion is `"model" in seat`, which is what the declared negative control reddens when the seat's model line is deleted; the substantive assertion at line 166 compares the rotation's result against the same seat key the accessor reads, so the negative control does not show that the resolution arm itself fails when the rotation stops reading the seat.

test_refine_default_holds_the_seated_tier replaces the previous "fallback must contain sonnet or opus" capability guard with a five-substring denylist, so a future cheap line outside those five substrings passes while the guard's stated purpose is to stop a capability downgrade.

the module README still documents the default model as anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, which this change retires by moving the compaction default to claude-haiku-5.5 at imas_codex/settings.py:201, so the documentation now disagrees with the code because of the landed change.

the latestness record cites a fetch time and per-line created epochs but the fetched 852,517-byte model list is not preserved with the fragment, so no later reader can verify the epochs or check which releases each line held at that moment.

the gate the manifest's tests line names runs pytest only, so the done_when's "every seat resolves to its new identifier with a non-null price, shown in the gate log" and the per-identifier completion probe appear in sibling logs instead; resolve-seats.log also ran at revision 88aeaf639, before the pricing commits 6da5cd1db and 92096c2ab that finalised the catalog.

the run's landing record names head commit 92096c2ab, while the reviewed head is 1bad1af53 and two further commits touch the same seats and their guards, so a reader of the landing record cannot tell what revision the promoted tree will hold.
